system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Normal monomorphism
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Cover normal monomorphisms of dendroidal sets via free tree-automorphism actions on complements, their recognition on non-degenerate dendrices, normal and non-normal examples, relative skeletal cell attachments, and the closure and boundary-generation properties established here. Exclude later model structures and the separate tensor-product preservation problem.

ATOMS:
- MATH-TOP-C04-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: A monomorphism $u: X\to Y$ of dendroidal sets is called normal if, for every tree $T$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(T)$ acts freely on the complement $Y_T - u(X_T)$ of the image of $u$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0137-s27] More generally, a monomorphism u: X →Y of dendroidal sets is called normal if for each tree T the group Aut(T) acts freely on the complement YT −u(XT) of the image of u.
- MATH-TOP-C04-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: A dendroidal set $X$ is normal precisely when the inclusion of the empty dendroidal set $\emptyset\to X$ is a normal monomorphism.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0138-s02] Thus, X is normal precisely if the inclusion of the empty dendroidal set  →X is a normal monomorphism.
- MATH-TOP-C04-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: The class of normal monomorphisms of dendroidal sets is the smallest weakly saturated class containing the boundary inclusion $\partial\Omega[T]\to\Omega[T]$ for every tree $T$, because every normal monomorphism is a transfinite composition of pushouts of such boundary inclusions.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0145-s09] Theorem 3.31 The class of normal monomorphisms is the smallest weakly saturated class containing the boundary inclusion ∂Ω[T] →Ω[T] for every tree T in Ω.
    [MATH-TOP-p0145-s14] To see that these classes are equal one ap- plies Proposition 3.26, which shows that any normal monomorphism can be written as a transﬁnite composition of pushouts of boundary inclusions of trees. □
- MATH-TOP-C04-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: If $A\to X$ is a normal monomorphism of dendroidal sets, then for each $n\ge 0$ the relative skeleton $\mathrm{sk}_n(X,A)=A\cup \mathrm{sk}_nX$ is obtained from $\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}(X,A)$ by a pushout of $\coprod_{(T,x)}\partial\Omega[T]\to\coprod_{(T,x)}\Omega[T]$, where the coproduct ranges over isomorphism classes of pairs $(T,x)$ with $T$ having $n$ vertices and $x\in X_T$ a non-degenerate dendrex not in $A_T$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0142-s04] Proposition 3.26 Let A →X be a monomorphism of dendroidal sets.
    [MATH-TOP-p0142-s05] If it is a normal monomorphism, then for each n ≥0 there is a pushout square
    [MATH-TOP-p0142-s07] g Ý(T,x) Ω[T] skn(X, A).
    [MATH-TOP-p0142-s08] The coproduct ranges over isomorphism classes of pairs (T, x) whereT has n vertices and x ∈XT is a non-degenerate dendrex not contained in AT.
- MATH-TOP-C04-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: Normal monomorphisms of dendroidal sets are closed under composition, pushouts, retracts, coproducts and sequential colimits (each $A_i \to A_\infty$ is normal if each $A_i \to A_{i+1}$ is), and also under pullback along a normal monomorphism, so they form a saturated class.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0143-s04] Proposition 3.28 (i) If A f−→B and B g−→C are normal monomorphisms, then so is their composition g f . (ii) If A C
    [MATH-TOP-p0143-s06] is a pullback in which C →D is a normal mono, then A →B is a normal mono as well. (iii) If A →B is a morphism of dendroidal sets and B is normal, then A is normal as well. (iv) If A C
    [MATH-TOP-p0143-s08] is a pushout in which A →B is a normal mono, then C →D is a normal mono as well. (v) If A u−→B is a retract of C v−→D, i.e. if there exists a commutative diagram
    [MATH-TOP-p0143-s12] in which ri = idA and sj = idB, then u is a normal mono whenever v is. (vi) If {Ai →Bi}i∈I is a family of normal monomorphisms, then their coproduct ⨿i Ai →⨿iBi is a normal mono as well. (vii) If A0 →A1 →A2 →· · · is a sequence with colimit A∞for which each Ai →Ai+1 is a normal mono, then each Ai →A∞is a normal mono as well.
    [MATH-TOP-p0145-s06] Thus, the previous proposition implies that the normal monomorphisms form a saturated class of morphisms in dendroidal sets.
- MATH-TOP-C04-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: The terminal dendroidal set $N\mathbf{Com}$ is not normal, whereas the representable dendroidal sets $\Omega[T]$ and the dendroidal set of planar structures $\mathrm{Pl}\cong N\mathbf{Ass}$ are normal.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0138-s06] Example 3.23 (a) Any representable dendroidal set Ω[T] is normal.
    [MATH-TOP-p0138-s10] By Proposition 3.13 it follows that α is the identity. (b) The dendroidal set of planar structures Pl NAss is normal. (c) The terminal dendroidal set NCom is not normal. (d) Example (b) is a special case of the following general fact.

  ATOM: If $P$ is a $\Sigma$-free operad (each symmetric group $\Sigma_n$ acts freely on the set $\mathbf{P}_n(-;c)$ of $n$-ary operations into each colour $c$), then its nerve $N\mathbf{P}$ is a normal dendroidal set.
